text:
anna: FYI restore job spiked failures for tenant-998 snapshots. Error shows 'decrypt: missing-kms-metadata' in logs. Anyone?

devon: I grabbed the head-object on one of the keys. Metadata contains x-enc-mode: sse-c and x-amz-server-side-encryption: AES256. Our expected header is x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms.

marco: Timeline: deploy of uploader v2.3.1 at 2026-03-21T02:00Z had an RBAC tightening on the uploader service account. Could be related. @lina did the change remove access to secrets or KMS?

lina: I scoped down iam:secretsmanager:GetSecretValue for uploader to a narrower secret path. I thought it only affected credentials rotation. Pulling deploy diff now.

anna: First failures at ~2026-03-21T02:03Z, ~3 failures in quick succession then stopped. Restore bot shows KMS.DecryptDenied in two cases.

restore-bot: restore tenant-998/snap-20260321 -> FAILED
error: KMS.DecryptDenied: missing-grant
s3-meta: x-enc-mode: sse-c

devon: Audit logs for PutObject lack KMS GenerateDataKey and Encrypt calls for the timeframe. That suggests uploader skipped rewrap to CMK and uploaded with SSE-C fallback.

marco: If uploader defaulted to SSE-C, those objects are encrypted with client-supplied keys. We don't have those keys unless they were proxied through our secrets. Ephemeral grants won't help for true SSE-C objects.

lina: Confirmed: the uploader codepath checks env KMS_KEY_ARN; if missing it falls back to SSE-C using a locally generated one and doesn't persist it. The RBAC change prevented reading the KMS ARN from Secrets Manager so fallback triggered. Oops.

anna: Immediate containment: 1) block v2.3.1 uploads via autoscaler tag 2) push a hotfix to remove SSE-C fallback 3) create detection to find objects with x-enc-mode: sse-c.

marco: For detection I'm going to run a parallel head-object sweep for all tenant prefixes touched in that window. Pseudo: `aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket archive --prefix tenant-998/ | jq -r .Contents[].Key | xargs -n1 -P20 aws s3api head-object --bucket archive --key` -> grep header.

devon: I'll correlate PutObject CloudTrail entries with EKS pod metadata to see which uploader instance wrote them. If keys were client-provided externally (i.e., customers), we may need to request key material from them.

lina: Opening a sec-ops approval ticket for a short-lived KMS grant in case some objects did call KMS but grant timing blocked decrypt. Note: ephemeral grant only helps if object was actually re-encrypted with our CMK.

anna: Compliance: if any of those objects used customer-supplied keys and we can't decrypt, escalate to SOC + legal. We need a timeline, impacted object list, and whether any external IPs were involved.

restore-bot: Created incident INC-20260321-2 — severity P2.

marco: I'll take owner of the head-object run and produce CSV. ETA 40m.

devon: I'll add a Live Query to detect future PutObject events missing aws:kms header and alert. Also enabling a fail-open to block uploads from the broken uploader image in the registry.

lina: Fix planned: revert RBAC scope that removed secret read for uploader, plus remove fallback and add runtime assert that KMS_KEY_ARN exists. CI will add a test for x-amz-server-side-encryption header.

anna: Action items: lina -> RBAC rollback + PR; marco -> head-object sweep and one manual restore attempt if sec approves ephemeral grant; devon -> audit correlation + live query; anna -> compliance comms and incident writeup.

marco: Quick note on mitigation commands I plan to run locally:
```
# list suspect keys
aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket archive --prefix tenant-998/ --start-after "snap-20260321" --max-items 1000 | jq -r .Contents[].Key > /tmp/keys.txt
# parallel head to gather metadata
cat /tmp/keys.txt | xargs -n1 -P30 -I{} aws s3api head-object --bucket archive --key {} --query '{Key:Key, Metadata:Metadata}' >> /tmp/metadata.log
```
marco: Will redact PII from CSV before attaching to incident.

devon: Reminder: add an audit entry for any ephemeral grant created and retire it immediately after usage. Record the IAM principal who requested it.

lina: Filed PR to remove SSE-C fallback (link attached in incident). Will also add a smoke test in deploy pipeline to detect missing KMS env.

anna: Good. Keep updates in the incident thread and ping oncall if we need expedited approval for grants. We'll run a short postmortem after containment. :thumbsup:
